newsitem.title: USA: White House sees little backing for CPI panel.
newsitem.headline: White House sees little backing for CPI panel.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday that the idea of forming a bipartisan commission to determine possible changes to the consumer price index (CPI) "has not been warmly received" in Congress.

McCurry was commenting on a Washington Post report that said President Bill Clinton had abandoned the idea of establishing an independent panel to reduce the cost-of-living adjustments for social security and other federal benefits.
"There doesn't seem to be enthusiasm for a commission," McCurry said. "That doesn't mean that there aren't other ideas that might work....That may not be the only way to skin the cat."
McCurry declined to say how the White House might choose to approach the issue.

There appears to be consensus among economists that the CPI overstates inflation but there is little agreement on how to go about addressing the issue. The subject is politically sensitive because many popular federal benefits are indexed to the CPI.
